introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The twenty-eight-day courtship season ends. Whatever you learned, there is no royal wedding waiting at the end of this attempt.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The final day cannot be retrieved with a clever message, an extra training session, or a conveniently timed browser refresh.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "I would like to appeal the deadline."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: An official stamps your appeal *RECEIVED* and immediately stamps a second page *DENIED.*

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: It is a disappointing ending, but it does not erase the choices you made. Your journal remains available until you choose to restart or begin a new route.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: **Ending: The Courtship Window Closes.**

meta.Type: Terminal failure, shown following expiration of Day 28 without a successful marriage.
meta.END: Preserve terminal failed run and journal. No automatic restart. Offer separately confirmed Restart Current Route / Start New Route and read-only review access. Existing unlocked gallery endings remain intact. No playable Day 29.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Last night, you were a software engineer staring at another rejection email. The subject line began with *Unfortunately* and ended before your hope did.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "I'm beginning to think the job market has been balanced by a particularly mean game designer."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Then the world folded like a poorly tested user interface, and you fell into a kingdom with more castles than entry-level openings.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A public notice welcomes travelers to the royal courtship season. You have twenty-eight days to form a genuine bond with the princess whose path you choose. The season's deadline will not wait for anyone's perfect speech.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "I was hoping for a recruiter, but all right."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The royal notice offers practical advice: build your skills, watch the weekly schedule, and remember that the person you're trying to impress can say no.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Finally, an application process with clear requirements."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The first morning begins. Your chosen route awaits.

meta.Type: Introductory, no time cost. Played after starting a newly named route, before the first regular gameplay action.
meta.END: No journaled gameplay action, stat reward, relationship gain, or time advancement; transitions to Day 1, morning. The 'courtship season' framing of the deadline is a **proposed new lore detail** requiring approval.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The Palace Court has prepared a wedding ceremony with thirteen banners, nine trumpets that nobody will sound today, and a document confirming that both parties consent of their own free will.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "The consent document is excellent. We should consider removing the trumpets from future events as well."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "The court seems rather proud of them."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "The court is welcome to marry the trumpets."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A few guests laugh. Others look surprised that the princess they've feared for years is quietly amused by her own ceremony.

introLines.speaker: HERALD
introLines.text: "Do you, Princess Kaedra, choose this partnership of your own will?"

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "I do. I remain guardian of the people I serve, and I choose {PLAYER} as my partner—not my subject and not my keeper."

introLines.speaker: HERALD
introLines.text: "And do you, {PLAYER}, choose Princess Kaedra of your own will?"

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "I do. Including the days when she comes home from saving the kingdom and wants five minutes of silence."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "Ten minutes. I have negotiated the terms."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The court records your vows. Kaedra keeps her strength, her wings, her duties, and a little more freedom to show the tenderness she has always possessed.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Later, in the Royal Gardens, she sits close enough for your shoulders to touch. Nobody asks her to stand guard over anything for a moment.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "There will still be frightening days. And days when I get things wrong."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "We'll tell each other when we need help. And we'll still be ourselves."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "That is precisely what I wanted."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She rests her forehead against yours, a gesture of affection with no audience, no grand magic, and no requirement to be brave about it.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "For the record, you should know our children will not be permitted to study ceremonial speechwriting until they're old enough to refuse."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "How many children is this hypothetical policy for?"

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "I have no intention of approving a figure before the relevant committee has met."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: You both laugh. For once, the silence afterward is neither fear nor duty. It is simply home.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A young messenger whispers urgently to a nearby court attendant. Whatever has been seen, the account grows two extra horns by the time it reaches the third listener.

introLines.speaker: MESSENGER
introLines.text: "A monster was seen near the royal paths. Great armored back, enormous claws, impossible stare. The princess was nearby!"

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "I have only the usual number of horns. Please keep that part accurate."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "What did they actually see?"

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A small, moss-backed garden creature emerges from behind a low step, carrying a fallen blossom on its head like a ceremonial crown. It has no weapon and appears mainly interested in a patch of shade.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "Oh. There you are."

introLines.speaker: MESSENGER
introLines.text: "You know it?"

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "It lives near the gardens. It once stole a judge's lunch and left the plate very clean. The court considers this an act of political commentary."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Is it dangerous?"

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "Only to unattended sandwiches."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The creature steps toward a busy walkway. Kaedra calmly asks people to give it room and points out the shaded route back to its usual resting place. Nobody needs to draw a weapon.

introLines.speaker: MESSENGER
introLines.text: "So there was no monster attack."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "There was a rumor. People can be frightened by rumors. That part matters even when the story is foolish."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She watches the small creature amble off, then notices you have stayed beside her rather than joining the speculation.

options.labelText: "You protected the people who were scared and made room for a harmless creature. I wish they'd notice that instead of turning both of you into monsters."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "That is more or less what I was trying to do."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "The sandwiches may disagree."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Their concerns have been entered into the record."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Kaedra smiles without glancing around to see who is watching.

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "I cannot control every story about me. But I can choose how I act. It helps to have someone notice the difference."

options.labelText: "It's just a ridiculous rumor. Ignore everyone, and the whole thing will disappear."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "It may. The fear people felt does not become unreal because its cause was mistaken."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I was trying to make it sound less serious."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Sometimes I need you to take me seriously without making me a tragedy."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She leaves the messenger to straighten the story while she returns to her duties.

options.labelText: "Why bother reassuring them? You're frightening, and so is the creature. Let the villagers be afraid."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Fear is not a service I provide."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I didn't expect you to take offense."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Then you have not been paying attention."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She sees the little creature safely away and ends the conversation.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A royal prince has arranged a traveling display of ceremonial cloaks. He is loudly explaining why an embroidered cape should be classified as an emergency public service.

introLines.speaker: PRINCE
introLines.text: "The garment makes a statement. Ideally, the statement is *behold my significance*."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "My own cape makes a statement too. It says *someone forgot to account for door handles*."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "You sound experienced."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "I once disabled an entire banquet by turning around too quickly. The curtains fell. Three ministers interpreted it as a declaration of war."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The prince freezes in admiration. A guard behind him inches toward a convenient pillar.

introLines.speaker: PRINCE
introLines.text: "Princess Kaedra! A demonstration from our most formidable guest would lend tremendous prestige. Perhaps you could look terrifying while wearing the silver mantle?"

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "Does the mantle require anyone to look terrified, or merely the audience?"

introLines.speaker: PRINCE
introLines.text: "Whichever photographs better."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A few spectators wait for Kaedra to explode. She doesn't. One wing settles against her back; the tense silence is otherwise broken only by a tailor dropping a pin.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "I was invited to assess whether the formal fasteners are safe. They are not. The weight is pulling on the collar."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "And the prince wants you to model it?"

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "He believes my face could frighten the stitching into cooperation."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Kaedra glances toward you, her expression composed. She has made it clear she would rather be heard than displayed.

options.labelText: "You were asked for your judgment, not to serve as a scary decoration. Want me to help make sure they hear the safety issue?"

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "You heard the part about the collar."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I also heard the part about the curtains. That's a separate safety issue."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Correct. We should not confuse the two departments."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Kaedra explains the flawed clasp without raising her voice. The tailor fixes it; the prince announces the resulting adjustment as the latest court trend.

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Thank you. I can speak for myself. It helped that you gave me room to do it."

options.labelText: "You should wear the cape and show them your legendary terrifying pose. At least it would be funny."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "It might be funny for you."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I thought you liked jokes."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "I do. I prefer knowing I am in on them."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She quietly takes the loose clasp to the tailor herself. The display proceeds, but she offers you no further performance.

options.labelText: "They should be afraid of you. Threaten the prince until he does what you say. That's what you're good at."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "No. I am good at making sure nobody has to be afraid."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "That wasn't what I meant."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "It was what you asked me to do. Please remember the difference."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She turns back to the tailor and ends the conversation without another word.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The conversation should be ending. Kaedra stays anyway. She looks at you with the same level gaze that has silenced entire rooms, but there is no court to impress here.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "You are remarkably difficult to intimidate for someone who once described this kingdom's employment prospects as 'a hostile deployment environment.'"

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "The description remains accurate."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "And yet you kept returning."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A comfortable silence follows. Her wings remain folded, her tail resting still, and for once neither of you needs to fill the quiet with a performance.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "There is something I want to say before you assemble a ceremonial argument for why I'm supposed to be impressive."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "I had three pages prepared."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "Then we may still have time to prevent a disaster."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "I enjoy protecting people. That is not a burden I secretly want someone to lift from me. But sometimes I come home tired. Sometimes I am unsure. I want to be able to say so without a room going silent."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "You should be able to."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "I have been called a weapon, a guardian, and a legend. I would rather be someone's equal. A person they can disagree with, laugh with, and trust to make her own decisions."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Kaedra reaches toward you, then stops a little short. She is not afraid of rejection because she is weak. She is afraid because this answer matters to her.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "I care for you. More than I expected. I do not need you to be fearless around me. I only need you to see me clearly."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Kaedra..."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "If this is a proposal, please do not begin with a list of my strengths. I know most of them already."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The three carefully rehearsed pages suddenly seem less useful than one honest sentence.

options.labelText: "I love your strength, and I love the gentleness you choose when nobody is watching. You don't have to protect me from every uncertainty, and I won't try to take your decisions away. I want to share an ordinary life with you as well as the extraordinary parts. Kaedra, will you marry me—as my equal?"

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "An ordinary life?"

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "Well, ordinary by this kingdom's standards. We may have to live with a few royal speeches."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "I can endure them if I am allowed to object to the page count."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Her expression softens. She takes your hand, careful not to treat it as something delicate or something to hold captive.

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Yes, {PLAYER}. Not because you need a guardian, and not because I need someone to command my life. Because I choose you, and you have chosen me."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I think I can live with that."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Good. Your proposal passed inspection. Barely."

options.labelText: "You're the greatest guardian who ever lived. I'd worship you every day. Marry me and I'll never question anything you decide."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "I don't want devotion that makes you disappear."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I thought you would appreciate being admired."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Being admired is not the same as being known. I want someone who can tell me when I'm wrong."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She gently lets go of your hand. The conversation ends, but not all hope does.

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I wanted to make things easier."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "I want room to rest, not someone who takes away my life and calls it kindness."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Kaedra steps back. She is not angry at the existence of your feelings, only at the bargain you tried to make with hers.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Kaedra greets you without a formal bow. There is relief in the familiarity, but also a question neither of you has answered yet.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "I have thought about your proposal. The answer matters enough that I won't pretend we understood each other."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "I've been thinking about it too."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "I don't want to be a legend you kneel to. And I don't want a guardian appointed to protect me from myself. Can you see a life with the actual person standing here?"

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She waits steadily. The silence is not a threat; it is room for you to choose your words.

options.labelText: "Yes. I was wrong to make you into a symbol or someone I needed to manage. I love you as you are: capable, sometimes tired, kind, and free to make your own choices. Will you marry me, and let us build a life where we can both speak honestly?"

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "You have learned to make a short speech."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Please don't."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Yes, {PLAYER}. I choose you. As an equal, and as myself."

KAE-MID-01.title: The Royal Trial (first full midpoint attempt)

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The Palace Court has arranged a formal ceremony called the Royal Trial. Its stated purpose is to recognize the kingdom's guardians. Its unofficial purpose appears to be finding out how much bronze can fit on a podium.

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "This is the sixth speech praising my ability to stand still. I fear my greatest talent has been misidentified."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Do they know you have others?"

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "One day, I may demonstrate sitting."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A herald invites Kaedra to lift a ceremonial warding sigil above the platform. Its light is meant to be symbolic, a brief ceremonial flourish.

introLines.speaker: HERALD
introLines.text: "A gentle flame, Your Highness. Just enough for the audience to admire the court's protection."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "Understood. Keep the aisle clear."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Kaedra raises one hand. A narrow band of amber light traces the sigil—then an unexpected spark snaps sideways and pops against the empty edge of the stone platform.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Nobody is struck. A nearby attendant flinches, and several people crowd toward the same exit, tripping over one another in their hurry. The spark dies before it can reach the banners.

introLines.speaker: HERALD
introLines.text: "Remain calm! Please move away from the platform in an orderly—oh dear, that's my shoe."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "That was not the pattern I intended."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Kaedra lowers her hand at once and extinguishes the sigil. Her wings stay folded. You can see that her immediate attention is on the crowded aisle, not her own embarrassment.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "The spark is out. People are bunching up by the doorway."

introLines.speaker: KAEDRA
introLines.text: "Yes. They saw it. They saw me lose control for a moment."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The situation is small but real: frightened people need a clear exit, and Kaedra needs the dignity of being treated as a responsible person rather than a spectacle.

options.labelText: "Let's give everyone room and ask the attendants to clear the aisle. Your magic is already stopped. Once they're safe, can we talk somewhere quiet?"

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "Yes. Tell the herald the side aisle is clear. I'll check the platform."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: You help direct the crowd away from the platform while the attendants open an unobstructed route. Kaedra verifies the sigil is extinguished and that nobody is hurt. The remaining onlookers settle.

branchLines.speaker: HERALD
branchLines.text: "The ceremony has concluded. Perhaps we will resume the speeches after an interval of several years."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: Later, beneath an arch **within Palace Court**, Kaedra stands with her arms folded, not to threaten anyone but to steady herself.

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "When the spark went sideways, I knew how to stop it. I also knew what everyone would think. That I had finally become the danger they expected."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "The spark was unexpected. You stopped it, checked on people, and took responsibility. You can be shaken by that without it defining you."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "They ask me to be a shield. A shield, apparently, is never permitted to be frightened."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "A person can protect other people and still need somewhere safe to speak honestly."

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "I was afraid you'd admire the spectacle. Or come here to tell me I need protecting from myself."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I came because I care what you're feeling. You decide what happens next."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The muscles around her jaw loosen. She exhales, long and slow, no longer measuring every breath against a watching court.

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "That is an alarmingly sensible answer. I may be forced to invite you to future ceremonies as a precaution."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "Does it come with fewer speeches?"

branchLines.speaker: KAEDRA
branchLines.text: "No promises I cannot keep. But I could ask you to stay a little longer."

options.internalLabel: Correct; midpoint completed; zero heart change

options.labelText: "That flare was incredible. Forget the crowd—show them an even bigger one and they'll respect you."

introLines.text: "I've told them three times that the currents are not assigned tables."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Nerelle waits at the waterline in the same pearl-and-ocean-blue royal outfit she chose to wear, her single teal tail moving quietly beneath the surface. No spell changes her form, and nobody asks her to leave her home behind.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "I have an announcement before we begin. I've arranged my responsibilities with the council. I'll continue to serve the ocean court and to make journeys when I choose."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A murmur rises from the sea guests. A stern-looking court official takes out a list, hesitates, then adds a new heading: *Arrangements Actually Discussed With the Princess.*

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "I see reform is already spreading."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Should I give a speech about our unprecedented cross-cultural scheduling achievements?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "You prepared a speech?"

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Only twelve pages. I cut the appendix."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "How merciful."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: When the formal promises begin, neither speaks about surrender. They speak about asking, listening, remaining honest, and finding each other across the places where land and sea meet.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "I choose you, {PLAYER}. I choose my people, my home, and the questions I haven't asked yet. Thank you for never making me pretend those choices cancel one another."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "I choose you, Nerelle. And I hope you keep telling me when I'm wrong about a current."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Then we should enjoy a long marriage. You're wrong about currents quite often."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Later, beside the Gardens canal, Nerelle drifts at ease in the water while you sit on the bank. Beyond you the kingdom remains complicated, beautiful, and unfinished.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Do you think we planned enough?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Enough to begin. We can decide the rest together."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: The water carries the reflection of two figures toward the open channel. Neither has to become the other to share a future.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Ribbons trail from the quay railing. In the water, little floating lanterns bob beside the canal, bright with painted names and small wishes. In daylight, their patterns catch the sun; at dusk, their lights begin to glow.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Welcome to Moonwater Festival. Our official explanation says the lanterns honor those who guided us home. The unofficial explanation is that everyone enjoys making something float and then pretending it is a solemn tradition."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Both can be true."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Exactly. You are getting dangerously good at this."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A group of young sea-dwellers carefully guides a string of lanterns along the water's edge. Nerelle exchanges a practiced greeting and listens to their questions with complete attention.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "They seem glad you're here."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "I love this part of my responsibilities. They come to me with genuine concerns. I can sometimes help."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "And the parts you don't love?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Those still exist. I used to think the answer was to accept every demand until there was no room left to want anything. Now I'm trying to learn which duties are mine, which I can share, and which are merely habits dressed as laws."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A lantern drifts into an eddy, circles twice, and points upstream as if it has decided to attend a different festival.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "That one has achieved more independence than half the royal council."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Does it get to decide where it's going?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Not entirely. Currents are real. But we still choose how to travel with them."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "I want to keep serving my people. I also want to keep learning about yours. Sometimes people hear one wish and assume it cancels the other."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She watches the lanterns, then turns back to you. She has told you what matters; now she wants to know what you heard.

options.labelText: "You don't have to abandon your people to make room for your own life. You can decide what duties matter, where help is possible, and which discoveries you want to make. I'll listen to what you choose."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "It's a surprisingly large relief to be understood without first providing a twelve-page petition."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I can provide a form if that would help."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Don't tempt me. I know several excellent forms."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She steadies the wayward lantern with a small movement of her tail, turning it back into the shared channel instead of fixing it in place.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "My place in the sea matters to me. So does the part of myself still becoming something new."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "Those both sound like parts of you."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "They are. And I would like anyone close to me to love the whole of that."

options.labelText: "Why not just appoint someone else to do the ceremonies? Then you could spend all your time exploring."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Some responsibilities can be shared. Others matter to me personally."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I thought that would make things easier."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Perhaps. But I don't want a future that's easier because half of who I am has been removed."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The festival carries on around you. Nerelle thanks you for trying, though the conversation ends before she can explain everything.

options.labelText: "All these lanterns and speeches seem pointless. Your people would manage without you, so why pretend the duties matter?"

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "They aren't pointless because you haven't learned why they matter."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I didn't mean to insult them."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Then please stop talking as if being important to others means being unimportant to myself."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She joins the festival-goers in the water. You are not asked to follow the conversation further.

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A line of small waterproof parcels floats beside the canal railing, each tied to a ribbon so precisely that a court clerk might weep with envy.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Do you have a moment? I've been conducting an extremely unscientific study of surface souvenirs. The findings are troubling."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "How troubling?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "You sell seashells to people who already live beside the sea. Then you charge extra if someone has written *Authentic Ocean* on them."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "That's the advertising industry. I used to live in a world with an advanced version."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Advanced? Can it convince a fish it needs to buy water?"

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Give it a few fiscal quarters."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Nerelle laughs, then nudges one parcel toward the stone lip of the quay. Inside is a polished bit of sea glass beside a neatly folded sketch of a harbor lantern.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "A child in the tide villages gave me the glass. She said it looked like the surface lights when the water is calm. I wanted to understand what she meant."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Did you ask her?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "I did. She was shy when she recognized me. Sometimes a crown makes an ordinary question feel like an examination."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "So I'm trying to learn how to be curious without turning people into a royal research project. My current theory involves fewer official seals."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She holds out the sketch for your opinion but watches your expression more closely than the paper.

options.labelText: "Maybe ask what matters to them, then listen without trying to decide what the answer should be. We could start with the lanterns if you'd like."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "The astonishing art of allowing a question to remain a question."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "They don't teach it in the advanced advertising industry."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Their loss."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She studies the reflection of a lantern in the water. Her tail fin shifts beneath it, sending the light into a dozen small shapes.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "The child wasn't explaining the lantern. She was telling me what home looks like from below."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "That sounds worth remembering."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "It does. For once, I shall not commission a commemorative plaque."

options.labelText: "The important thing is that souvenirs are symbolic. Let me explain the entire surface economy of sentimental objects."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "That sounds informative. It's not quite what I was asking."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "Sorry. I thought more information would help."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "It may. But if I wanted a lecture, I'd have invited the royal tax assessor."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She keeps the child's sketch tucked safely beside her and returns to the water as the conversation ends.

options.labelText: "How can you be a princess and still need someone to explain ordinary surface things?"

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Because I am a princess of the sea. I rather thought that distinction was visible."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Not knowing your customs is not the same as lacking sense."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She closes the parcel herself. The polite farewell that follows is considerably shorter than the conversation she had hoped for.

NER-FIN-01.title: A Future She Chooses (first full final proposal)

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: As the conversation ends, Nerelle does not swim away. She rests one hand on the waterside stone and looks across the familiar meeting place as though seeing it anew.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "You've become rather good company for a surface traveler. That's not a compliment I award lightly. My standards include knowing which end of a boat belongs in the water."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Both ends, ideally."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "You're improving."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She laughs, but her attention turns serious. Under the water, her fin settles against the current instead of hurrying her away.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "There is something I need to tell you before you say whatever you've been rehearsing."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "I might have rehearsed nothing."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Then this may be our most efficient conversation yet."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "I have spoken with the people responsible for my duties. I can share some of the work. I will keep the responsibilities I believe are mine. And I'll continue exploring the surface-facing waterways when I choose."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "How did that go?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "With many documents. I believe three council members grew new gray hairs during the discussion."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "There will be disagreements. Some days my people will need me. Some days I'll need quiet. None of that makes me less interested in a life with you."

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "I do not want to leave the ocean to become someone else's idea of a proper bride. Nor do I want to ask you to surrender your life and call it devotion."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "What do you want, then?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "A partnership we choose, with honest plans, places to meet where water reaches the shore, and room to keep learning. Not every question has to be solved in advance."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She reaches her hand up from the water, not as someone waiting to be rescued but as someone inviting you to answer as an equal.

options.labelText: "Nerelle, I love your curiosity and the way you care for people. I love that you know what matters to you. I don't want to choose your future for you. Would you marry me and keep choosing how we build it together?"

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "You really heard every word."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I tried. I expect I'll need reminders."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Good. I've already prepared several, in alphabetical order."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: For a moment she looks out to the water, where the tide keeps moving. Then she turns back on her own terms.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Yes, {PLAYER}. I would choose that life with you. The ocean is still my home. My duties will still be real. But there's room for us, if we keep making that room honestly."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I don't know every part of what comes next."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Neither do I. I used to think that meant I'd failed to plan."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "And now?"

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Now I think it means we get to write a few pages together. Please use waterproof ink."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes your offered hand across the waterside stone. Neither of you needs a transformation or a grand rescue to make the answer real.

options.internalLabel: Correct; terminal success, gallery unlocked, no additional heart bonus

options.labelText: "Marry me, and I'll find a spell to give you legs. Then none of these complications will matter."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Legs?"

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "So we could live together on land."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "You heard me tell you who I am, and answered with a plan to change it."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I thought it would be easier."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Easier for whom? I cannot say yes to a future that begins by erasing mine."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She does not treat the question as a joke, and she does not agree. The possibility of speaking honestly again remains, but the answer today is no.

options.labelText: "I'll abandon everything above the water for you. We'll never have to think about the surface again."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "You'd give up your entire life because you think I need you to?"

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "That's what devotion is, isn't it?"

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "No. Not for me. I want both of us to remain people with lives and choices, not to become proof that love requires disappearance."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The tide moves softly between the quay stones. She leaves you with an honest refusal and the chance to ask with a different understanding.

NER-MID-01.title: The Forbidden Journey (first full midpoint attempt)

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Nerelle is waiting in the water below the quay, unusually quiet. A folded chart rests on a dry ledge within her reach, weighted beneath a smooth stone.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Before you ask: no, I have not stolen a map. It belongs to me. The court has simply declared it a terribly inconvenient object for me to own."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Is this where the official warning says 'forbidden journey'?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "It says 'unsanctioned surface observation.' If you enlarge the lettering enough, it sounds almost respectable."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She lifts a hand to the chart. The familiar water-accessible places near Moonwater Quay and the Royal Gardens canal are marked as possible surface-viewing stops: places close enough to hear markets and watch people going about their day.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "I know those currents. I know the tides and the places where the barges pass. I've helped guide emergency supplies here. Yet when I ask to visit simply because I want to, the answer changes."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Your court doesn't want you to go?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "They want me to be safe. They also want me to be available whenever a council member discovers another urgent meeting. Both things are reasonable until there is no time left that belongs to me."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: A surface courier crosses a nearby bridge carrying a stack of documents taller than his head. The top sheet escapes and lands in the canal. Nerelle catches it before it sinks.

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "The surface, meanwhile, is defending itself with administrative paperwork. I feel at home already."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Why tell me about the journey now?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "Because I trust you, and that makes this harder. Everyone has an opinion about what I should do. I wanted to hear yours. I'm afraid you'll give me another order, even if it comes dressed as kindness."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "What do you want?"

introLines.speaker: NERELLE
introLines.text: "I want to learn how people live above the water. I want to remain answerable to the people who rely on me below it. And I want the choice to be mine."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: She waits beside the quay, tail resting in the steady current. The chart stays between you, open to amendment rather than demanding obedience.

options.labelText: "Then let's design a visit you actually want. You choose the route and when you're free of court duties. We can plan a safe waterside stop, agree on how you tell your court, and change plans if the tide or your responsibilities need it. I'll help, but it's your call."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "You didn't begin by telling me what I was allowed to do."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "You already know these waterways better than I ever will. I can help with the surface part."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Then here is what I propose. First, I finish my scheduled hearings. Second, I tell the appropriate attendants where I'll be. Third, I explore the garden canal because I want to, not because a task requires it."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "And if someone decides a private afternoon is scandalous?"

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "I'll ask whether they prefer their scandals alphabetized."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She traces the waterway on the map. You suggest where a surface walkway runs alongside it; she corrects you where the current is too swift.

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "I worried you would make this into a daring rescue. I don't need to be carried away from my life. I need space to live it."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "Then we make space, together."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Together. That sounds less frightening when you say it without deciding the rest for me."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: They follow the familiar canal waterline for a short distance, comparing its sounds and sights. Nothing about the route is new. The novelty is that Nerelle chose to take it.

options.internalLabel: Correct; complete milestone, no hearts gained

options.labelText: "You shouldn't have to deal with all this. I'll arrange everything and get you away from the court before anyone can object."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Away from the court? Those are my people. My responsibilities."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I only meant to free you."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "Free me to do what you've decided? I wanted you to hear my plan, not replace it."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She takes back the chart, leaving the conversation unfinished rather than agreeing to a future chosen for her.

options.internalLabel: Wrong; midpoint incomplete, no hearts changed

options.labelText: "Your court has a point. There are risks, so you should stop asking to visit the surface."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE
branchLines.text: "I know the risks. I came because I thought we might discuss them as equals."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "I don't want you hurt."

branchLines.speaker: NERELLE

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Someone in the Town Square has erected a tiny stage. A hand-painted sign announces: *Royal Comedy Showcase: Participation Voluntary, Embarrassment Inevitable.*

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: "Excellent. Finally, an event whose organizers understand their audience."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Are you performing?"

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: "I volunteered yesterday. Today I'm thinking I'd rather be a person in the crowd."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR
introLines.text: Onstage, a wizard pulls a rabbit from a hat. The rabbit takes one look at the audience and pulls the wizard back inside.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "Tough act to follow."

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: "The court expects me to be effortlessly brilliant. I don't want to be brilliant on command. But I don't want to disappoint everyone, either."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "What do you actually want?"

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: "That is becoming a rather dangerous question around you."

options.labelText: "Then don't perform. We can watch terrible jokes together. If you decide to go onstage, I'll cheer. If not, I'll still be here."

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: "I think I'd like to stay. Just stay."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: The next comedian announces that his act is entirely improvised and immediately reads from a scroll marked *Entirely Improvised Act.*

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: "I may have found the only performer in the kingdom less spontaneous than you."

branchLines.speaker: PLAYER
branchLines.text: "That was spontaneous and hurtful."

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: "And I didn't need a whole stage for it."

options.labelText: "You always make people laugh. You'll feel better as soon as you're onstage."

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: "Maybe. But it would have been nice to decide that myself."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She delivers a competent routine. Everyone applauds. Tavri thanks them, and her smile fades as the crowd disperses.

options.labelText: "Backing out makes you look weak. A real princess wouldn't disappoint her audience."

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI
branchLines.text: "I was hoping I could be myself for once. Now I have another audience to disappoint."

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR
branchLines.text: She steps away from you and joins the crowd alone.

introLines.speaker: PLAYER

introLines.text: "Finally, a scholar who understands modern sorcery."

introLines.speaker: NARRATOR

introLines.speaker: TAVRI
introLines.text: "If I joke about it first, perhaps nobody will notice I'm bothered. That's the usual plan."

introLines.speaker: PLAYER
introLines.text: "And if the plan isn't working?"

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI

branchLines.speaker: NARRATOR

branchLines.speaker: TAVRI

help.title: First Steps
help.text: You have 28 days in the royal courtship season. Each day has morning, afternoon, and evening. A valid action uses one slot; looking at menus and Help does not. Select the princess whose story you want to pursue.

help.title: Finding Her
help.text: The princesses have different repeating weekly schedules. Check the calendar before attempting a conversation. An unavailable meeting cannot become an extra visit.

help.title: One Conversation
help.text: You can speak to your selected princess once on an eligible day. A conversation uses one slot even when you choose an answer she dislikes.

help.title: Training Basics
help.text: Your four stats are Charisma, Intelligence, Strength, and Kindness. There are two approved training activities for each. Levels one through five require one training session each; levels six through ten require two sessions each.

help.title: Five Hearts
help.text: Five hearts is an intentional story gate, not a broken meter. Once your requirements are met, the next eligible princess encounter brings a pivotal conversation. The requirements panel shows what is missing.

help.title: Preparation Needed
help.text: The next pivotal conversation is waiting for preparation. Check the visible primary and secondary stat requirements and train as needed. Looking at this notice costs no slot.

help.title: Try Again Later
help.text: That was a consequential answer, not a command error. The midpoint did not complete; hearts were not additionally penalized. Another eligible day offers the shorter follow-up.

help.title: Ten Hearts
help.text: An ordinary or optional encounter that reaches ten hearts continues directly into the approved proposal scene. It is part of the same encounter, not a new day or extra slot.

help.title: A Better Proposal
help.text: An unsuccessful proposal leaves your relationship at ten hearts and a later-day follow-up pending. Keep an eye on the remaining calendar.

help.title: Last Days
help.text: The 28-day deadline is real. Resolve any pending milestone or proposal while you still have an eligible scheduled encounter. The last evening is playable; there is no playable Day 29.

help.title: Unexpected Moments
help.text: Some princess moments are optional and can be missed. Explore naturally; you do not need every optional story to reach marriage.

help.title: Saving Progress
help.text: The game keeps local progress and offers explicit backup/export and recovery options. Read the displayed save status before leaving. If saving reports a problem, use the recovery guidance without assuming the progress was safely stored.

help.title: Recovering a Save
help.text: If a backup import or recovery fails, do not overwrite a working save merely to retry. Read the validation error and choose the recovery option that preserves the most reliable existing state.

help.title: After the Deadline
help.text: A failed courtship ends the run, but the journal remains available until you explicitly confirm a new start. Losing does not silently erase the record of your choices.

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY
squareQuips.text: “The palace insists every problem has a committee. I prefer problems that have a chair.”

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY
squareQuips.text: “When a mermaid tells you the water is the right place for her, I would recommend believing the expert.”

squareQuips.speaker: HUMPTY

lines.text: You exchange pleasantries with the townsfolk, learning how often a simple question works better than a polished entrance.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Nobody asks for a performance review, which counts as progress of a different kind.

lines.text: You compare two careful accounts of the same obscure custom and notice where the writers disagree.

lines.text: A useful answer now has room for a better question.

lines.text: The enchanted oracle offers an answer with three footnotes and a warning that its confidence is decorative. You check the references.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The oracle politely admits that “probably” is not a proof.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You finish a measured set of bodyweight exercises, treating steady form as more important than impressive noises.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The floor survives another training session.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You practice controlled movements using the guild’s ordinary training equipment. Nobody has to fight anyone.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The training target remains intact; this is considered a success.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You offer patient attention to the garden dogs and make sure they have water and a comfortable place to rest.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A wagging tail offers an eloquent but entirely nonnumeric review.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You collect stray scraps around the square, leaving the paths and flowerbeds a little better than you found them.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The square has one fewer mess and no added parade in your honor.
